races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Jimmy Murray Agri Services Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Blue Anthem
runners_data.note: 4yo prominent racer trained by Gerard O'Leary, showed a solid fifth on similar good ground 43 days ago; headgear (hg:t) may sharpen focus and this trip and surface suit — Shane Foley booking is an asset in a race this size.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Veteran 10yo but landed a second on good ground over 8f recently with Seamie Heffernan aboard; consistent placed form on this surface (9/15 sim-going) backs him to travel prominently and grind out a finish if the pace is steady.

runners_data.name: Methgal
runners_data.note: 4yo who has hit the frame twice on soft and on standard, but trainer P J F Murphy has just 0 wins from 8 runners in the last 14 days — apprentice claim could help offset the OR; watch for a prominent pitch that fades in the final furlong given the form drift to fourth last time.

runners_data.name: Givehertilxmas
runners_data.note: 168 days off the track is a serious fitness query for a hold-up horse that has failed to place on any going at a comparable trip; the 3lb claim from Jack Kearney helps but the long absence and zero placed form on good going make this very hard to assess.

runners_data.name: La La Lucrative
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground 25 days ago showing clear aptitude for this surface and trip, but the repeated ⚠ fades-in-finish flag suggests she needs a true pace to chase down — Matthew J Smith's yard has one win from 11 runners in 14 days, so form is mixed.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in nine good-ground runs and steps back from a 9f good-ground third recently, suggesting the 7½f trip is not a problem; hold-up style in a race where closers face an uphill battle, but Denis Hogan's in-form team (2/19 in 14 days) provides some trainer confidence.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: 8yo hold-up type whose last win came over 7f on heavy/soft; genuinely races at the back but with the rear end overcrowded, is mapped to midfield — its natural closing style makes it hard to benefit from a steady pace, and the fades-in-finish flag is an additional concern.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: 4yo with a win over 8f on good ground but form has gone backwards since (699), and the 56-day absence adds doubt; a true hold-up runner whose chances diminish in a shape where closers cannot reach their optimal position.

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Recent fourth over 8f on good ground in the latest is positive, but Dylan Browne McMonagle's eye-catching booking aside, the horse wears a visor (hg:v) and finished 13th in two of five starts — its natural hold-up style is forced into a midfield role by the congested rear.

runners_data.name: Snap Decision
runners_data.note: Limited data (all finishes outside top 7, best an 8th), 87 days off the track, and no sim-going win record — the redistribution out of a true hold-up role further limits scope, and this looks a very difficult task from a form perspective.

runners_data.name: Alandownunder
runners_data.note: 3yo consistent backmarker — nine placings or worse in last five, all on good or good-to-soft; the fades flag plus a field shape that denies the back position makes progress unlikely, though the first-time blinkers angle (hg:b) could theoretically sharpen early.

runners_data.name: Polanco
runners_data.note: 3yo with a string of double-figure finishes in five recent starts on good going; trainer P F O'Donnell has just one runner in 14 days, no momentum, and this horse's running style is squeezed out of a genuine hold-up role it relies upon.

runners_data.name: Misava
runners_data.note: 2yo stepping up in grade and trip after 364 days off the track — Noel Meade's yard is active (2/19, 14 days), but the year-long absence combined with a true hold-up style remapped to midfield makes a winning performance highly unlikely first time back.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Newark
runners_data.note: 3yo with a third on good ground over 8f as best form, and the step up to 7½f from shorter is untested — hold-up type pressed into midfield, but the Wesley Joyce 3lb claim and the Matthew J Smith yard's in-form status (1/12 in 14 days) offer some marginal appeal.

runners_data.name: He's Holding Court
runners_data.note: Has a fourth over 8f on good ground recently and a run of finishes that show gradual improvement; Andrew Slattery's yard is active (2/21, 14 days) but the hold-up style and the forced midfield berth mean any run will come from the wrong part of the field for this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Selective Power
runners_data.note: 7yo with two fourths on good ground including over 8f, so the surface and distance are fine; genuine hold-up horse whose racing style fits naturally, but the redistribution note is absent here — still, fades-in-finish flag and 0 wins from 5 similar-going starts suggest a placing rather than a win.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is an unusual flag 16 days out from a run; best form is a third on good ground over 7f last year, and hold-up style with a pulled-up last run makes this hard to support — the sim-going record of 5/6 runs in the frame positions is misleading given actual finishing positions.

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with a clear path, but recent form reads 040850 and the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] tag indicates it is being asked to perform in a prominent/lead role that may stretch its ability to control and quicken — the uncontested lead is the asset, recent finishing positions are the liability.

races.paceDynamic: Eichan San is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival likely to push them from the front — this creates a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground over 7½f at Roscommon. The prominent trio of Blue Anthem, Brains, and Methgal will track closely behind, ensuring the pace is honest without becoming a genuine burn-up, which suits horses who can travel within themselves before the home turn. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up types — Alandownunder, The Blue Panther, Polanco, Shahada Ace, Snap Decision, and others are genuine closers who cannot all find their natural position and have been redistributed on the map; of these, Alandownunder and The Blue Panther are most likely to actually press towards the rear of the main group given any residual forward intent. A single, unsustainable pace-setter producing a steady gallop on good turf over this stamina-testing 7½f favours prominent racers who can track economically and pounce inside the final two furlongs — hold-up horses face the additional burden of racing out of role and closing into a pace that may never truly string out the field.

watchPoints.text: Eichan San's uncontested lead is the single biggest tactical factor in this race — if Terry Casey elects to coast through slow fractions unchallenged, the prominent chasers Blue Anthem and Brains must judge their challenge perfectly or risk being outfoxed by a horse with nothing to beat.

With 18 runners in a 0-60 handicap, the draw and early positioning battle could see several horses denied their natural pitch — Blue Anthem, Brains, and Methgal all need to establish prominent ground quickly or they risk being swallowed up in traffic on a track where getting past rivals is difficult.

La La Lucrative's win 25 days ago on good ground over 7f is the most recent, directly relevant piece of positive form in this field — if the pace is honest enough to suit a hold-up runner, she cannot be ignored despite the fades flag.

Medieval Night's trainer Denis Hogan has 2 wins from 19 runners in the last 14 days and the horse steps back from 9f to 7½f on a surface it clearly handles — monitor market moves as this is the type of quietly improving horse that Hogan's operation can place well in large-field handicaps.

Misava (364 days off the track) and Givehertilxmas (168 days) are both significant fitness unknowns in a field where freshness should be questioned — if either shows unexpected early zip, it will distort the anticipated pace shape.

races.name: Conor Cassidy Car Sales Handicap

runners_data.name: Iamimmaculate
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and likely to get a dream uncontested lead; 255-day absence is a flag but trainer O'Leary has a poor 14-day strike rate and the solo pace could paper over fitness cracks — the style fit of 0.90 caution is less relevant when she is literally the only leader.

runners_data.name: Adel
runners_data.note: Won last time at 12f on Good and steps back slightly in trip but has course-relevant form; a genuine hold-up horse whose style is honestly suited here — 43 days since last run with trainer O'Callaghan in modest form.

runners_data.name: Honouramongthieves
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator who needs a strong tempo to be effective; recent form shows consistent finishes in 5th-7th and Good ground suits, but the absence of a contested pace undermines the profile here.

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: Strong prominent racer who ran 2nd-2nd-3rd in last three starts over 8-10f; Ben Coen is a key booking, the step to 10f suits, and racing close to a single front-runner plays to his strengths — just 8 days since last run warrants a minor flag.

runners_data.name: Rapide Vega
runners_data.note: Hold-up type equipped with a hood; Good ground is a positive with a sim-going record of 3/5, but needs the pace honest enough to close and that is not guaranteed against a sole, untroubled leader.

runners_data.name: Freedom And Light
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type in terms of race style, but the redistribution to midfield signals the map cannot place all the rear-runners honestly — Bolger's 0-from-7 14-day record and a record of 7th-6th-4th-8th-9th suggest limited upside regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose position in the map overstates his access to the front; a run of 7th-11th-7th-6th-6th and trainer Mullins 0-from-6 in the 14-day window make it hard to construct a winning case.

runners_data.name: Second Line
runners_data.note: Carries a headgear flag (blinkers) and a fade-in-finish warning alongside redistribution concerns — mapped to midfield but naturally wants to come from off the pace; a sequence of 6th-8th-8th-10th and apprentice booking limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Dont Get Me Wrong
runners_data.note: Prominent racer tagged with a fade-in-finish warning; won at 7f on Standard and steps up in trip and class here, with a 50-day absence and trainer O'Leary without a 14-day winner — interesting profile at the weights but finishing suspect.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a solid record of placed efforts (2nd-2nd-2nd) and a 3lb apprentice claiming; Good ground suits with 4 sim-going runs from 7, and racing close to a steady pace gives her a chance to sustain her effort to the line.

races.paceDynamic: Iamimmaculate is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm from the off over this 1m2½f trip on Good ground at Roscommon. Nermal, Dont Get Me Wrong, and Ella's Gold will push to track closely in a small prominent group, while the hold-up contingent — Adel, Honouramongthieves, Rapide Vega — will settle further back seeking a late run. This field carries more hold-up horses than the track map can honestly accommodate at the rear: Vantage Code, Freedom And Light, and Second Line are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield, meaning they are unlikely to find the ground or gaps their style demands and their chances in a late-pounce shape are structurally compromised. The race shape — a single leader setting a measured, sustainable pace on Good ground — tilts firmly in favour of prominent-racking horses who can travel close to the tempo and quicken off it, rather than those needing a strong gallop to come from well off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Iamimmaculate's 255-day absence is the single biggest unknown — watch whether she travels fluently in the early stages or shows signs of ring-rust that allow the prominent group to overwhelm her before the straight.

Nermal runs just 8 days after her last start — monitor how she moves through the field on the turn, as any sign of fatigue from a quick turnaround could undermine what otherwise looks a well-placed prominent runner.

Vantage Code, Freedom And Light, and Second Line are all genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield on the map — if the pace is steady, watch for traffic issues or lack of room as they all attempt to find the same gaps in the straight.

Adel is the one true hold-up horse with a recent winning form reference at this trip and going — watch whether McDonogh on Freedom And Light or Jamie Powell on Adel finds better daylight, as that separation may determine which closer lands a blow.
The Good ground is consistent across all race distances on the card today — no sectional variation or watering anomaly to factor in, so form at this level of going can be taken at face value.

races.name: Sean Cleary Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer from the G M Lyons yard, Jack Kearney taking the ride; has placed on good ground over nine furlongs but hasn't won in 26 days of preparation and faces a step up to 10 furlongs here — needs a fast-run race to produce his best late effort.

runners_data.name: Amplitude
runners_data.note: Sam Coen claims the five-pound allowance for a Joseph Murphy yard that is 0/11 in the last 14 days; hold-up style suits a genuine gallop and the horse has placed consistently at 12-13 furlongs on good, making the trip no concern, but the stable's recent form is a flag.

runners_data.name: Liam Swagger
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and tactically pivotal, returning from 422 days off for James Owen who has struck at 3/26 in the last fortnight; has won over 12 furlongs on good-ish ground and the tp headgear suggests he'll be prominent, but freshness after such a long layoff is a genuine unknown.

runners_data.name: Follow Me
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a hold-up type who has shown form over shorter trips on good, with the step back up to 10 furlongs and into handicap company after a 43-day break the key questions; trainer Ross O'Sullivan has been active and placed recently.

runners_data.name: Unterberg
runners_data.note: Laura Hourigan's seven-year-old arrives on a hat-trick of wins over 12 furlongs on standard going at Dundalk — the switch to good turf over 10 furlongs is an obvious query, but he travels prominent, the Mulligan apprentice claims five pounds, and the horse is in demonstrably the form of his life.

runners_data.name: Vlhova
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides this lightly-raced three-year-old who has placed at up to eight furlongs on soft and heavy; stepping into handicap company for the first time over 10 furlongs after 237 days off, the trip and going are unexplored territory that introduce real uncertainty despite a prominent style that suits the pace map.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who has run eight days ago on good ground and found little late, with a form string showing a run of modest efforts at 8-10 furlongs; Nicola Burns claims five pounds but the recent evidence doesn't suggest this horse is firing.

runners_data.name: Marta's Prince
runners_data.note: James Ryan rides a French-trained three-year-old with a limited UK/Irish form profile — the style is listed as unknown, last ran 234 days ago, and the stable's profile over 10 furlongs on good turf is opaque; the wildcard in the race.

runners_data.name: Sir Jeremy
runners_data.note: Noel Meade has landed one from 18 over the last fortnight, and this four-year-old won on good ground over 10 furlongs for Adam Caffrey, but its natural instinct is to race from the back of the field — with the hold-up berths overcrowded, it may find itself racing closer to the pace than suits its style, diluting the late punch it showed on that winning day.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning eight days after finishing fifth, with Rory Cleary in the saddle for a Coleman yard that is quiet lately; the form over 10-13 furlongs on good is decent and the prominent style is exactly what this race shape is calling for, though the horse has placed at the weights without winning regularly.

runners_data.name: Sinbad My Dad
runners_data.note: Seamus Fahey's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by pattern, having placed at both 10 and 12 furlongs on standard — returning from 158 days off with the J Harnett seven-pound claimer aboard, and while connections might try to cover more ground, the redistribution note tells the real story: there simply isn't enough room at the back for all the closers in this field.

runners_data.name: Flying Fortress
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell has been busy and hit one from 28, and this four-year-old wears a hood, has won over eight furlongs on heavy and placed over 10 on good; prominent by style, returning 18 days on from a midfield finish, and the 10-furlong trip on good turf aligns reasonably with its profile.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Matthew Smith's four-year-old won back-to-back in 2024 but hasn't run in 237 days, and carries the PaceMap ⚠ fade flag on top of the redistribution note — despite winning twice over shorter distances, its true closing style means it would need a searching gallop to fire from the back, and returning from such a layoff compounds the risk.

races.paceDynamic: Liam Swagger is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the early lead — this sets up a solo, uncontested gallop at a sustainable rather than pressured tempo across 1m2½f on good ground at Roscommon. Vlhova, Unterberg, Thatwilldoso, and Flying Fortress will push forward to dispute the prominent positions behind Swagger, creating a small cluster of tracked runners rather than a true pace battle, which means the overall tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle in their natural position at the rear: Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, and Blackjack Hills are genuine closers by preference but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the hold-up berths are oversubscribed — in practice these horses may find themselves closer than ideal or unable to generate the late momentum their style demands. A solo leader setting a steady, uncontested tempo on a flat track in good ground classically favours prominent racers who can track the pace from a ground-saving position and pounce in the straight, rather than deep closers who need a genuine end-to-end gallop to reel the field in.

watchPoints.text: Unterberg's hat-trick of wins is all on Dundalk standard — watch whether Shane Foley can get him settled prominently on good turf over 10 furlongs, a sharply different surface and trip combination that could expose a limitation not yet seen.

Liam Swagger's 422-day absence means his fitness level is unknown on debut for the race; if he goes too hard from the front in the early stages, the whole pace map collapses and a faster-run shape emerges that helps closers who cannot ordinarily secure their position.

With Sir Jeremy, Sinbad My Dad, and Blackjack Hills all genuine hold-up types competing for the same ground at the rear, watch for traffic issues in the straight — bunching at the back could see legitimate staying-on finishers unable to find a clear run when they most need it.

Vlhova races for the first time in 237 days over a distance and going she has not encountered in handicap company — if she settles prominently under Shane Foley she is tactically well-placed, but the combination of first run back and trip extension is worth monitoring in running.

Dylan Browne McMonagle on Follow Me is an elevated rider for a horse that has not won at seven furlongs or beyond in recent form — watch whether the jockey opts to use the hold-up style or whether McMonagle positions more prominently, which would be a significant in-running signal.

races.name: Watch Racing TV Irish EBF Lenebane Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Chally Chute
runners_data.note: Lightly-framed prominent racer in excellent recent form (two wins from last four, including a Listed success), well handled by a competent apprentice; only 11 days since last run but connections clearly believe he's in a good place, and Good ground over 1m4f suits his profile perfectly.

runners_data.name: Starford
runners_data.note: High-class performer at a mile for Joseph O'Brien now stepping up in trip for Dylan Browne McMonagle; 53 days off and his best form is at shorter, so the 1m4f is the key question here, though his prominent style fits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Counting Coup
runners_data.note: Front-runner whose sole 2024 outing produced a win in Soft; heads to Good ground here and that could temper his speed, but he will push to lead and dictate, setting the table for those behind him.

runners_data.name: Shaool
runners_data.note: Consistent but has yet to win at 1m4f; Ben Coen takes the ride and he brings in a prominent to midfield style that can benefit from a strong pace, though the headgear and six weeks off suggest he needs conditions to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Abbey Actress
runners_data.note: Good recent form including a win 19 days ago; her natural inclination is to race prominently, but the front-running duo leaves her squeezed for position and she is likely to find herself tracking from further back than ideal — a minor discount to her winning chance as a result.

runners_data.name: Bosphorus Rose
runners_data.note: Two wins from 12 outings on Good ground make her a live contender on going; like Abbey Actress she is a front-running type by nature but will be unable to secure that position with Counting Coup and Dreamkeeper ahead of her, and W J Lee will need to make decisions early.

runners_data.name: Kalixa
runners_data.note: 271 days off the track is the dominant concern here; she showed ability in a Listed context when last seen and the 1m4f trip is within her compass, but fitness after nearly nine months away is a major question mark for M D O'Callaghan's filly.

runners_data.name: Dreamkeeper
runners_data.note: See above — covered in front-runner note.

races.paceDynamic: Counting Coup and Dreamkeeper are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 1m4f trip at Roscommon, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than an uncontested soft lead. With two horses intent on setting the fractions, the gallop should be honest if not pressurised, and those racing behind in a prominent or close-tracking position — particularly Chally Chute and Starford — are best placed to exploit the tempo without burning energy in the early battle. Bosphorus Rose and Abbey Actress are natural prominent racers who are unlikely to secure that slot cleanly given the pace already ahead of them and have been mapped to midfield as a consequence; the position closest to the front runners will be contested ground. This race shape, with a genuine dual pace scenario on a flat, fair track in Good ground, strongly favours a well-rated prominent or close-tracking racer who can track the leaders under cover and pounce from a winning position in the straight without expending early energy.

watchPoints.text: Counting Coup and Dreamkeeper will both push for the lead — watch the first two furlongs to see whether one capitulates early or whether both trade genuine fractions, as this determines how quickly the race is truly run.

Bosphorus Rose and Abbey Actress are natural prominent racers who may find themselves shuffled into unfamiliar midfield positions in the first half-mile; if either is unsettled by the lack of a clear early run, their chance is compromised before the race reaches its critical phase.

Starford steps up significantly in trip from his best form at a mile — watch his jumping off/travelling through the final turn, as any sign of him not staying the extra ground would be a significant early indicator for punters with interests.

Kalixa's 271-day absence means her early behaviour and how she travels through the first half of the race is the most informative data point about her fitness; a horse carrying that much ring rust rarely wins first time back from this kind of layoff at Listed level.

The Good ground is reported consistently across all distances at Roscommon tonight — no rail bias concern reported, and the flat track should ensure the pace scenario plays out without any significant topographic distortion favouring wide or inside positions.

runners_data.name: Black Heather
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse rated OR 120 with solid good-ground credentials and a 451-day absence to overcome; despite the REDISTRIBUTED tag placing it in midfield, its true role is to come from off the pace, and in a moderate-tempo race that compression may partially compensate for the positional compromise — though the long layoff is a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Coolnagrattan
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo with only one recorded run on good ground but the services of Seamie Heffernan and a 14-day trainer strike rate of 1/5 that suggests a live chance; the unknown-style flag and minimal data make this genuinely hard to assess, but top rider bookings in maiden company carry meaningful weight.

runners_data.name: Cracking Cloud
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up markedly in trip from 10f to 14f having finished 3rd-5th-6th in recent starts, with no soft-ground concerns on today's Good surface; the trip extension is the key question, but tracking Boujee from a handy position suits the style entirely.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a single 16f good-ground run to its name (13th) and a fades-in-finish flag that points to stamina limitations at this distance; the 67-day absence and moderate form profile makes it hard to see this winning from the rear.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: OR 71 hold-up type with a scatter-gun form profile across varying surfaces and distances, mapped into midfield through redistribution rather than genuine positional choice; the 107-day absence, poor recent form (740-0) and tendency to race on fast ground away from turf good make this a longshot.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with the fades-in-finish flag and two consecutive last-place finishes on Good ground at 10f before a 2nd over 16f on Heavy — the step back to Good and up to this trip is contradictory form evidence, and the 29-day return does not resolve those questions.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type returning 12 days after a 7th on Good ground, carrying the fades-in-finish flag and a modest sim-going record of 8 wins from 10 comparable runs — actually a mixed record that flatters the stat, with no win in recent form string and a wide trip range suggesting inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Quint Major
runners_data.note: OR 120 hold-up horse with solid experience at 16f on Good ground (1 win, 3 placed from 9 comparable runs) and a 264-day absence; the return from a long layoff is the primary concern, but if fit enough the good-ground mile-and-a-half profile is genuine.

runners_data.name: Seti One
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with fades-in-finish flag, poor recent form (84000-) and a REDISTRIBUTED positional tag pushing it into midfield away from its natural rear draw; the long 193-day absence and limited good-ground turf experience make this a very difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on a blinkers switch (hg:b) stepping up from 10f with a 2nd on Standside recently; the headgear application and booking of W J Lee for A Oliver suggests the yard is trying to sharpen focus, and the prominent style is ideally placed to exploit Boujee's steady gallop from just off the leader.

runners_data.name: Ashikita
runners_data.note: Rated OR 120 but holds the REDISTRIBUTED tag, meaning its true closer's style is compressed into a midfield map position in this field; with only two career starts and a modest 5th on 12f good ground, the lack of experience at this trip in a 16-runner maiden is a notable concern despite the Murtagh/Coen combination.

runners_data.name: Boujee
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer confirmed as the sole front-runner, carrying the STYLE_FIT note that tempers enthusiasm — returning from 335 days off (25 days since a hurdles run), the ability to control this race at a sustainable tempo is genuine, but the age and long flat absence raise durability questions in the straight.

runners_data.name: Catherine Magennis
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo with only a 7th on Soft to her name, making today's Good ground an unknown; Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking for Joseph G Murphy in an open maiden signals stable confidence, and the unknown style leaves tactical options open for a jockey of that calibre.

runners_data.name: Grennanstown Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with four starts at 18f on Good ground in her recent history (best 4th), suggesting genuine stamina but an inability to quicken when it matters; today's trip of 14f may actually be shorter than ideal, and the 56-day break is neutral.

runners_data.name: Sioux Grit
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse returning from 773 days off carrying the fades-in-finish flag and REDISTRIBUTED positional tag; the extreme layoff, OR of just 32 and poor recent form history make this a no-hoper in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer equipped with a visor (hg:v), returning quickly (11 days) after an 8th on Soft with a 2nd on Good at 12f and a placed effort on 8f; the step up to 14f is a question mark, but the visor, quick return and prominent style are all positive tactical signals in a race where the leader will be there to track.

races.paceDynamic: Boujee is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 1m4f maiden and, with no rival willing or able to press for the lead, will dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Roscommon. Cracking Cloud, Steel Cut and Taj Crown are the prominent types most likely to track Boujee closely in the early positions, creating a compact lead group rather than a strung-out field. The moderate, uncontested tempo Boujee sets will compress the field and compress the finish, meaning the race is unlikely to be truly run until after halfway, benefiting those who can travel within striking distance and quicken from a handy position. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and mid-division horses with a turn of foot over true hold-up specialists, as the lack of genuine pace means those anchored at the back will simply face too much ground to make up. The field contains considerably more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear — Black Heather, Ashikita, Seti One and Sioux Grit are all genuine closers who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their natural rearward position, diluting their ability to produce their best racing profile.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Boujee is actually allowed to stride clear unchallenged at the start — if Cracking Cloud or Taj Crown press more aggressively than expected, the entire pace dynamic shifts from controlled to contested, which would fundamentally alter which scenario plays out.

Black Heather's 451-day absence is a significant concern despite the OR 120 rating — watch the market move closely, as a hold-up horse returning after over a year needs to be sharply ready to feature from a compromised midfield position in this shape.

Steel Cut's blinkers application for the first time is a key variable — if the headgear sharpens focus this horse is perfectly positioned to track Boujee and produce a telling challenge, but blinkers first-time can also lead to erratic early behaviour in a 16-runner field.

Coolnagrattan and Catherine Magennis are both lightly raced with top jockey bookings (Heffernan and Browne McMonagle respectively) — watch for market confidence signals in the build-up, as unexposed horses with elite riders can outrun their data in maiden company on Good ground.

The sheer volume of redistributed hold-up types (Black Heather, Ashikita, Seti One, Sioux Grit) means the midfield will be unusually crowded; watch for traffic issues and interference in the straight as these horses attempt to find racing room from positions that are not their natural home.
